title: Viamédis TP for opticians: professional portal, coverage approval, statuses, and payment
metaDescription: Viamedis TP for opticians: contracting, the viamedis.net professional portal, optical coverage approval, statuses, and payment. Verified facts, with sources.
contentHtml:
Viamedis is a third-party payment operator: it pays the optician on behalf of more than 75 supplementary health insurers. In optical care, Viamedis TP works through a coverage request, entered on the viamedis.net portal before the equipment is dispensed. Third-party payment (tiers payant: the patient pays nothing upfront, insurers pay the provider directly) is the mechanism that spares the customer from advancing the reimbursed share: the optician is paid directly by the organization. Here, the share concerned is that of the AMC (supplementary health insurance, meaning the customer’s supplementary health insurer, or mutuelle, or health insurance company).

In practice, everything happens in three stages: contract once, free of charge; get the insurer’s approval for each file; then bill and track the payment. This page goes through each of these steps based on what Viamedis publishes on its professional website and what our agents observe on the portal while processing optical files.

Key takeaways
  • Viamedis pays the optician on behalf of more than 75 supplementary insurers. Optical care is part of its third-party payment based on a coverage approval or quote.
  • Contracting is free: account on viamedispro.com, upload of administrative and banking documents, then activation of viamedis.net.
  • Payment is guaranteed for a customer holding a valid third-party payment card showing the insurer’s name, the plan, and the Viamedis logo.
  • An approval “sous réserve de pièces justificatives” (subject to supporting documents) requires an upload on the portal: quote, delivery note, prescription, and invoice.
  • Viamedis does not publish a payment timeline specific to optical care: track your payments in the payment history on viamedis.net.

What is Viamedis TP, and which insurers go through it?

Viamedis is a third-party payment operator founded in 2000: on behalf of its client supplementary health insurers, it handles direct payment to healthcare professionals, including opticians.

The volume is massive. According to the reference page published by Viamedis, the operator processed more than 94 million invoices in 2025 and paid out €3.2 billion in benefits. It has more than 280,000 partner healthcare professionals.

Optical care falls under what Viamedis calls its “tiers payant complexe” (complex third-party payment), along with hearing and dental care: services that go through a coverage request or a quote, not a simple invoice. This scope accounted for 4.9 million invoices and €1.9 billion paid out in 2025. For you, the consequence is simple: on Viamedis, a pair of glasses cannot be billed under third-party payment without the insurer’s prior approval.

When you submit an optical request, the viamedis.net portal has you choose the organization from a list of 122 supplementary insurers, as observed by our agents. It includes, for example, MGEN, IPECA, and Mutuelle Bleue. This list describes what the portal’s selector offers: it does not mean an insurer goes only through Viamedis, nor that all its contracts are attached to it.

The right reflex: before searching for the insurer in a list, look at the customer’s third-party payment card. If it is currently valid and shows the insurer’s name, the plan, and the Viamedis logo, the coverage request is made on viamedis.net. This card is also what the payment guarantee announced by Viamedis depends on.

If you want to know which portal matches which card, our page on third-party payment portals presents the main operators used in optical care and their respective roles.

How do you access the Viamedis professional portal?

Access happens in two stages: a one-time contracting on viamedispro.com, then a daily login to viamedis.net, the area where you manage your files. Contracting is free for the healthcare professional, according to Viamedis’s healthcare professionals page.

The 5 contracting steps

  1. Create an account on viamedispro.com. This is the onboarding website, separate from the file management portal.
  2. Upload the supporting documents. From your area, send your administrative and banking information.
  3. Receive the onboarding email. It arrives once Viamedis has checked your application.
  4. Receive the viamedis.net activation link. A second email is sent after your bank details are validated.
  5. Accept the contractual commitment. At your first login to viamedis.net, you accept the terms of the contractual commitment.

The two addresses are often mixed up at the counter. The rule to remember: viamedispro.com is for becoming a partner, viamedis.net is for working once you are a partner. The contact forms follow the same logic, which keeps you from writing to the wrong department.

Depending on the specialty, Viamedis states that onboarding is also possible through Inter-AMC. If your store has already gone through this channel, check with Viamedis whether direct contracting is still needed before starting the procedure again.

Logging in to viamedis.net

Each store logs in to viamedis.net with an email address and a password, then a code from an authenticator app, for example Google Authenticator. This is what our agents observe on the portal: two-factor authentication is always required.

This two-factor authentication has a practical consequence. The code is generated on a specific phone: if the only person who set it up is away, the store can no longer enter coverage requests. So decide as a team which device the app is installed on, and who can access it during opening hours.

For a group of several stores, each location has its own credentials. Keep an internal sheet that links each store to its login address, without ever writing down a password in plain text. If access is blocked, the channel provided for professionals who are already onboarded is the contact form on viamedis.net, presented in the last part of this page.

How do you submit an optical coverage request on Viamedis?

The optical coverage request is entered on viamedis.net, before dispensing, for a customer holding a valid Viamedis third-party payment card. The portal lets you check the customer’s eligibility in real time, then enter and track quotes, coverage requests, invoices, and reimbursements.

A coverage approval, often abbreviated PEC, is the agreement by which the supplementary insurer commits, before the purchase, to the amount it will pay for a given piece of equipment. Without this approval, the file cannot be billed under third-party payment on Viamedis. The most reliable method always follows the same order.

  1. Check the third-party payment card. Check the validity period, the insurer’s name, the plan, and the presence of the Viamedis logo.
  2. Check eligibility in real time. On viamedis.net, confirm that the customer is indeed covered on the day of the request.
  3. Choose the organization in the selector. Select exactly the insurer printed on the card, not an entity with a similar name.
  4. Enter the request from the quote. Faithfully copy the equipment offered to the customer: lenses, frame, amounts.
  5. Track the answer until the final status. As long as the status is not an approval, the insurer has committed to nothing.
  6. Dispense, then bill. The invoice is entered on the same portal, once the equipment has been handed over.

The trap: the selector contains very similar names. For example, it includes MALAKOFF HUMANIS MUTUELLE, MUTUELLE MALAKOFF HUMANIS, and MALAKOFF HUMANIS PREVOYANCE, or several distinct NEOLIANE entries. Choosing the wrong line sends the request to the wrong administrator. Copy the label on the card, word for word.

The exact fields of the form may change as the portal evolves. The principle does not: the request must match the quote given to the customer, and the quote must match what will be dispensed. A mismatch between these three documents is the most common cause of blockage we see in the files handled by our agents.

When these requests run into the dozens every day and are spread across several portals, data entry becomes the store’s bottleneck. This is what Granit does: agents submit coverage requests directly on the platforms’ portals, including viamedis.net, then send the status back to the team. To place this step within the overall process, see our guide to third-party payment for opticians, from coverage approval to collection.

What do the statuses of a Viamedis coverage request mean?

A Viamedis status tells you what the insurer decided on your request and what you still have to do; the table below gives our agents’ reading of them on the portal.

Three statuses deserve particular attention, because they are misread at the counter.

“Accordée sous réserve de pièces justificatives” (approved subject to supporting documents)

This status is an approval, but not a complete one. The insurer commits on condition of receiving documents: the quote, the delivery note, the prescription, and the invoice, to be uploaded on the portal. Until these documents are uploaded, the file remains fragile. The right reflex is to prepare these four documents as soon as the order is placed, so you can upload them at billing time without searching.

“En attente”, “En instance”, or “En cours” (pending, on hold, in progress)

These three labels say the same thing: the file is still under review. There is nothing to correct, and resubmitting an identical request creates a duplicate. The action is to wait, then follow up at the right time. Viamedis does not publish a response time for optical care: set yourself an internal rule and record the request date in your software, so you know when to follow up.

“Expirée” (expired)

An approval has a validity period. Once it has passed, the status changes to “Expirée” and the approval no longer holds: you must submit a new request before billing. This mostly happens when the equipment is delayed (lenses on order, a customer who does not come back). Before dispensing, always check that the approval is still active.

The statuses “Annulée” (Canceled), “Close” (Closed), and “Supprimée” (Deleted) indicate a file that is no longer active: submit a new request if the customer is still buying. The “Facturée” (Invoiced) status shows that the invoice has gone out; tracking then shifts to the payment.

What should you do after a rejection or refusal?

A refusal is handled in three steps: read the reason displayed on the portal, fix the cause, then submit a new request. A “Refusée” (Rejected) status means there is no coverage approval as things stand, not that the customer will never get coverage approval.

We do not reproduce rejection codes here: a code only means something with its exact label, as the portal displays it at the time of the refusal. The reason is therefore the first thing to read, before any new entry. There are, however, a few causes to check every time, because they follow directly from the rules published by Viamedis.

Cause to checkWhere to checkFix
Third-party payment card expired or without the Viamedis logoCard presented by the customerAsk for the current card; without a valid card, the payment guarantee does not apply
Wrong organization chosen in the selectorLabel on the card and line chosen on viamedis.netSubmit the request again on the right line
Customer’s coverage rights not active on the day of the requestReal-time eligibility check on viamedis.netAsk the customer to check their situation with their supplementary insurer
Mismatch between quote, request, and equipment dispensedSigned quote, entered request, delivery noteAlign the documents, then submit the request again
Approval expired at billing timeFile status on viamedis.netSubmit a new request before billing

Keep a record of each step: the initial request, the reason for the refusal, the correction made, and the new request. If the refusal still seems unjustified after correction, contact Viamedis through the contact form on viamedis.net, citing the file and the exact reason. For the general logic of diagnosing a rejection, our article on reducing rejections without changing your practice management software offers a method you can transpose, even though it deals with the mandatory share.

When and how does Viamedis pay the optician?

Viamedis does not publish a payment timeline specific to optical care. The average 11-day timeline it announces concerns hospital third-party payment: do not apply it to your optical files.

What is published is a guarantee: Viamedis guarantees payment for policyholders holding a currently valid third-party payment card showing the insurer’s name, the plan, and the Viamedis logo. That is why checking the card, at the very start of the file, also protects your collection.

Payments are made to the account whose bank details were validated during contracting. If your bank details change, update them from viamedis.net, which lets you edit your details, before payments go out to an old account.

For tracking, viamedis.net gives access to the payment history. A file with the “Facturée” status is one whose invoice has gone out: that is the point from which you track the bank transfer. The most reliable method is to reconcile the invoiced files against the payment history every week, then against your bank statement. Our article on reconciling remittance files and bank transfers details a daily reconciliation routine you can adapt to optical third-party payment.

An invoiced file that does not appear in the history beyond your usual timeframe should be followed up. Since no timeline is published for optical care, your own history serves as the reference: record, store by store, the time observed between billing and payment.

How do you contact Viamedis?

The right channel depends on your situation: if you are already onboarded, use the contact form on viamedis.net; if not yet, the form on viamedispro.com. A phone line is also open on weekdays, at the rate shown in the card below.

Before calling or writing, gather the information needed to handle your request without back-and-forth: the store’s identifier on the portal, the file reference, the status displayed and, for a refusal, the exact wording of the reason. Never send the customer’s health data through a channel not intended for it.

For a problem affecting several platforms at once, our directory of third-party payment portals brings together the pages for the other operators, with the same structure as this page.

faqItems.question: How does an optician access the Viamédis professional portal?
faqItems.answer: You first contract, free of charge, on viamedispro.com by uploading your administrative and banking information. After checking the application and validating the bank details, Viamedis sends an activation link for viamedis.net. Each store then logs in there with an email address, a password, and a code from an authenticator app.

faqItems.question: Which supplementary health insurers (mutuelles) go through Viamédis for optical third-party payment?
faqItems.answer: Viamedis manages third-party payment for more than 75 client supplementary health insurers. On the viamedis.net optical portal, the organization selector offers 122 supplementary insurers, for example MGEN and IPECA. The customer’s card remains the reference: if it carries the Viamedis logo, the coverage request is made on viamedis.net.

faqItems.question: How do you submit an optical coverage request on Viamédis?
faqItems.answer: The request is entered on viamedis.net before dispensing, for a customer holding a valid Viamedis third-party payment card. Check the customer’s eligibility in real time, choose exactly the insurer printed on the card, then enter the request from the quote. The equipment is only dispensed once the approval is obtained.

faqItems.question: What do the statuses of a Viamédis coverage request mean (approved, pending, rejected)?
faqItems.answer: “Accordée” (Approved) means the supplementary insurer commits to the amount: you can dispense and then bill. “En attente” (Pending) means the file is still under review and you should wait before following up. “Refusée” (Rejected) means there is no coverage approval as things stand: read the reason, correct it, then submit the request again.

faqItems.question: How does a healthcare professional contact Viamédis?
faqItems.answer: A professional who is already onboarded uses the contact form on viamedis.net. A professional who is not yet onboarded uses the form on viamedispro.com. Viamedis also offers a premium-rate phone line, open Monday through Friday.

faqItems.question: How long does Viamédis take to pay the optician?
faqItems.answer: Viamedis does not publish a payment timeline specific to optical care. The average 11-day timeline it announces concerns hospital third-party payment. Payment is guaranteed for a customer holding a valid third-party payment card with the Viamedis logo, and tracking is done in the payment history on viamedis.net.
